chunks: Ali ibn Isma'il narrated from Fadala from Aban from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the female slave whom a man buys while she is pregnant, does intercourse take place with her? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.يَقَعُ عَلَيْهَا: Intercourse takes place with her (specifically referring to 'iqab' in slave context)

ai.seo_question: Can a man have intercourse with his female slave if she is pregnant?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the prohibition of *iqab* (intercourse) with a pregnant slave girl, a ruling derived from the principle of preventing the mixing of lineages (*ikhtilat al-ansab*). This specific prohibition highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving clear lineage and ensuring the mother's physical stability for the child's development, distinguishing it from general marital relations.
